talking_points: **Network-adequacy risk:** 33 solo primary-care physicians (age ~66+) in Washington are actively winding down, and 4 ZIP code(s) already have 2+ winding down at once — including Seattle (98104), Federal Way (98003), Bellevue (98004) — each a 12-month access-gap risk under Medicare Advantage and state drive-time standards.

**Facility-fee shield:** ~3,531 Medicare patients are attached to these winding-down practices today. If they drift into hospital-owned clinics, the plan pays 2-3x more per identical visit via facility fees. Corner NPs capture those panels at 85-95% of the physician fee schedule — a direct cost-containment shield.

**Auto-assignment targets:** the thinnest-supply counties — Island County — are where unattributed members and HEDIS gaps will concentrate as these doctors exit. They are prime spots to auto-assign members or co-fund outreach to a new Corner clinic.

**Immediate ask:** fast-track credentialing for Corner in Washington; 3 practice(s) are the highest priority (winding down with little local backup) and ~94,800 patients sit across all 79 at-risk solo practices statewide.
